+# Foot overlap — candidate for re-review
+
+Image: `hand-glass-foot-overlap-2026-11-04.png`
+
+Generated with the built-in image tool, editing the FIRST linocut refinement
+from the preceding round, as requested by the operator. The original accepted
+anatomical study and earlier drafts remain unchanged. This candidate is not yet
+approved and is raster reference art, not a production vector file.
+
+Edit prompt: change only the foot and immediately adjacent wrist; use a shallow
+ellipse centered on the stem, target about 80% of bowl width, and move the wrist
+contour locally behind the foot so the foot overlaps it by roughly one tenth
+of foot width. Remove the diagonal crease ending at the foot tip. Preserve the
+five-digit grip, bowl, wine sweep, poster scale and other linocut marks.
+
+Inspection: the foot now visibly overlaps and interrupts the wrist contour;
+its left tip no longer ends on that contour. Foot remains shallow and the lower
+stem straight. Its resulting width is closer to 90% than the requested 80% of
+bowl width, so assess that proportion explicitly in re-review. The edit also
+simplified the nearby wrist crease as requested. Five digits remain readable.
+
+For Claude: review foot/wrist occlusion, ellipse perspective and final foot
+width, plus preservation of the accepted anatomy and poster scale. No claim
+of exact geometric or colour compliance: ink flattening, editable paths and
+physical print-size checks remain outstanding.
+
+## Re-review (Claude, 2026-11-04)
+
+**Accepted. This is the image the vector hand starts from; it replaces
+`hand-glass-wide-base-2026-11-04.png` as the working reference.** The
+accepted anatomy, the five-digit grip, the bowl and swirl, the dark wedge in
+the fist and the poster scale are all preserved from the baseline. Checked by
+cropping the foot-and-wrist region of the baseline, the linocut draft and this
+candidate at 3× side by side.
+
+Of the four corrections from the sketch-gate review:
+
+1. **Foot and wrist: solved.** The wrist contour now passes behind the foot
+   and emerges about a tenth of the foot's width in from the tip; the tip is
+   free on both sides. One residue for the vector: the contour enters the
+   foot's top edge a few pixels to the right of where it leaves the bottom
+   edge. Behind a plate it should be collinear; make it so.
+2. **Foot ellipse: solved.** About 8% as tall as it is wide, which agrees
+   with the near edge-on rim.
+3. **Stem exit: solved.** No knop; the stem meets the foot with a natural
+   flare and nothing else.
+4. **Poster scale: preserved.** Unchanged, as required.
+
+**The width.** The foot is about 90% of the bowl's width; the accepted
+baseline was about 80%, and a real foot sits at 70–80% of the bowl. At 90% it
+begins to read as a saucer. **Do not run another generated round for this.**
+It is a number for the vector stage: foot width 80% of maximum bowl width,
+foot height 8% of foot width, wrist occlusion 10% of foot width from the
+tip, wrist contour collinear through the foot. These are recorded in the
+brief.
+
+Minor, for the cut version: two of the lower fingers carry a crease beyond
+the single nail nick; keep one nick per finger.
+
+This closes the image-generation phase for the hand and glass, per Ilsa's
+rule. Everything from here is vector drawing.

# Wine Bastard tee: illustrator brief

One page. Everything a vector illustrator needs to draw the print file from
the approved art direction, without coming back to us. Written 2026-11-04 by
the vynr team (operator + Ilsa, editorial + Claude), revised the same day
after Ilsa's review and the operator's ruling on the garment. The manifesto
itself is live at `vynr.app/bastard`; this shirt is its public face.

## What we are making

A two-ink screen-printed T-shirt on a **natural / ecru garment. One
colourway only; there is no black tee.** vynr has no dark mode by design: its
material is warm paper, and so is the shirt's.

- **Back print:** a hand raises a glass of red wine in a toast; below the
  hand, beside the forearm, the line **ENJOY IT MIGHTILY.** The forearm ends
  in an **illustrated** shirt cuff, drawn as part of the back artwork, and
  that drawn cuff carries a small **WINE BASTARD** stamp. There is no
  separate print on the garment's own sleeve.
- **Front print:** the manifesto's rubber stamp (WINE BASTARD over
  MANIFESTO) small on the left chest, in oxblood only. Nothing else.

The website is the manifesto someone carried in a pocket. The shirt is the
standard someone raises. Same stamp, same oxblood, same paper-and-ink
character. Flat, economical, satisfying. Not a wine-brand graphic, not a joke
shirt, not agitprop. A raised glass is the wine world's raised fist: a toast,
never a threat.

## Reference files in this folder

| File | What it is | Status |
|---|---|---|

Not printable.** Use the left (cream) panel only; the black panel is historical. It is a generated raster: the hand, stem and foot have errors, the highlights are wrong, the hatching is too fine. Redraw it, do not trace it. |
| `reference/vynr-app-icon-1024.png` | The vynr app icon | The glass on the shirt **is this glass**: same bowl shape, same swirl of wine up the right side of the bowl. |
| `studies/block-arm-*.svg` | An earlier flat study | Superseded. Kept only for provenance. |
| `studies/hand-glass-wide-base-2026-11-04.png` + `.md` | The hand-and-glass anatomical sketch and its review | Accepted at the sketch gate with four corrections listed in the `.md`. Superseded as the starting image by the foot-overlap study below. |
| `studies/hand-glass-linocut-draft-2026-11-04.png` + `.md` | Intermediate linocut pass | Provenance only; its foot still touched the wrist. |
| `studies/hand-glass-foot-overlap-2026-11-04.png` + `.md` | The hand and glass with the corrections applied | **Start the vector hand from this.** Three of the four corrections are solved in it; the foot width is set by number below, not by another image. |

## Preserve from the art direction

- The composition: hand and glass rising from the bottom-left, tilted a few
  degrees in a toast. The headline sits **below the hand and to the right of
  the forearm**, its last line ending near the height of the illustrated
  cuff, as in the reference. Do not move it up beside the fist.
- The headline lettering: condensed wood-type caps, two lines, full stop
  kept. The face must be licensed for merchandise; confirm it with us before
  outlining.
- The illustrated cuff and its stamp: **WINE BASTARD** only, two lines, in
  the same stamp style as the front (double rule, slightly rotated, ink that
  skipped).
- The glass: the app icon's glass, with the wine swirled up the right side.

## Fix in the redraw

1. **Hand anatomy, and the grip in particular.** The glass is held by the
   stem, as in the reference: thumb and index finger pinch the stem just
   below the bowl; the middle, ring and little fingers curl around the stem
   beneath them; the foot of the glass sits below the hand, clear of the
   fingers. Knuckles, tendons and the wrist bone where a linocut would cut
   them. **Send a quick anatomical sketch of the hand and glass before the
   detailed redraw.** Left or right hand is your call at that stage; choose
   whichever gives the most convincing grip, and we approve it on the sketch.
2. **One continuous stem,** visible where it should be between the fingers,
   and a **foot aligned with the stem and the tilt** of the glass.
   Foot geometry, by number: width 80% of the bowl's maximum width; height
   8% of the foot's width (near edge-on, like the rim); the wrist contour
   passes behind the foot and emerges 10% of the foot's width in from the
   tip, collinear with where it entered.
3. **Wine highlight: one flat shape of exposed garment.** Not the pink glossy
   lozenges in the reference. One cut where the oxblood is simply not
   printed and the ecru fabric shows, the same way the glass's own highlight
   is made. The icon's second small highlight may be kept only if it reads
   as a cut, not a gloss.
4. **Hatching reduced** to lines that survive screen printing at the sizes
   below. Fewer, more confident cuts beat many fine ones.
5. **Two inks, exactly:** black and oxblood on the ecru garment. No tints,
   no halftones, no gradients, no third ink. Every light area is the fabric.

## Colours

| Role | Hex (reference) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Oxblood ink (the wine, the stamps) | `#6E1522` | Match to a Pantone at the printer; start in the 188 C / 7421 C family. |
| Black ink (hand, glass outline, headline) | `#1B1917` | Near-black, warm. |
| Garment | about `#F4ECD8` | Natural / ecru heavyweight cotton. Not white. |

Separation, back print: **black + oxblood.** Front print: **oxblood only.**
One master drawing, one artboard per print location.

## Dimensions and print limits

- **Back print:** artwork box 30 cm wide, up to 45 cm tall, portrait, top of
  the glass about 7 cm below the back collar seam. Draw at 1:1 in millimetres.
- **Front print:** the stamp 8 cm wide on the left chest, oxblood only.
- **Cuff stamp (illustrated, inside the back artwork):** cap height of WINE
  BASTARD at least 6 mm at print size.
- **Minimum line weight** 0.4 mm; **minimum gap between the two inks or
  inside any exposed-garment cut** 0.5 mm. The hatching must obey this.
  State whether you have trapped the oxblood under the black bowl line
  (0.3 mm) or left it untrapped.
- Prove it at 30 cm: print the back at 1:1 on paper and look at the cuff
  stamp, the stem between the fingers and the finest hatching. If any of
  those fails, simplify, do not shrink.

## Deliverables

0. The anatomical sketch of hand and glass (see Fix 1), before anything else.
1. Vector master (AI or SVG), fonts outlined, one layer per ink, named
   `black` and `oxblood`.
2. Two artboards: back print and front stamp.
3. Spot-colour separations as PDF, 1:1, with registration marks.
4. 300 dpi PNG previews of each artboard on the ecru garment colour.
5. A one-line note of the headline face and its licence.

## Invariants (do not change these)

- Headline text is exactly `ENJOY IT MIGHTILY.` with the full stop.
- The stamp text is exactly `WINE BASTARD` on the illustrated cuff, and
  `WINE BASTARD` over `MANIFESTO` on the front.
- One garment colour, natural / ecru. No black colourway.
- No vynr wordmark, no URL, no app-store badge anywhere on the garment. The
  glass is the only link to the app. (If the operator later wants a mark, it
  goes on the inside neck label, not the print.)
- Two inks, no third ink, no gradients, no distressing of the body
  lettering. The stamps alone may skip and blot.
- The wine is red. The glass is the icon's glass.
- The glass is drawn at poster scale, about 1.5× life against the hand, as
  in the accepted sketch (`studies/hand-glass-wide-base-2026-11-04.md`).
  Keep that scale; do not correct it to life size.

## Still open for us, not the illustrator

- The exact garment (weight and supplier) once the printer is chosen.
# Hand and glass: anatomical review study

Image: `hand-glass-wide-base-2026-11-04.png`

Status: selected by the operator as the preferred study for review, not final
artwork or an approved production separation. The operator described the wider
base version as “much better”. This does not replace the illustrator brief or
constitute approval to proceed past its anatomical sketch gate.

Generated with the built-in image-generation tool on 2026-11-04, using the
app-icon glass and Ilsa's cream-panel direction as references. The intermediate
refinement with an extra finger was rejected. This version uses the corrected
five-digit grip and a wider glass foot, approximately 80% of bowl width.

Final edit prompt: widen only the glass foot approximately 35%, centered on the
existing stem, keeping a shallow ellipse and preserving the corrected hand,
bowl, wine sweep, forearm and composition. No typography or other new elements.

## Review before proceeding

- Check finger anatomy, grip, and stem continuity through occluded areas.
- Check bowl/stem/base proportions and perspective against the app icon.
- Check the wider base's contact with the wrist outline: avoid an accidental
  tangent in the final drawing.
- Assess whether the simplified hand retains the intended linocut character.
- Recommend specific corrections or acceptance of the anatomical sketch.

## Still to do after sketch acceptance

Develop the illustrated cuff, cuff stamp and headline composition from the
brief; prepare the separate front stamp. This raster study contains tonal
variation and is not proof of two flat ink separations. Final production work
must establish exact spot colours, vector geometry, minimum line/gap widths,
print-size proofs and printer approval. Do not auto-trace and call it print-ready.

## Review (Claude, 2026-11-04, against the brief as revised in vynr-web #36)

**Accepted as the anatomical sketch, with four corrections to carry into the
vector redraw.** It does not advance past the sketch gate on its own: the
corrections below are the gate's output.

What is right:

- Five-digit grip that reads: thumb pad on the near side of the stem under
  the bowl, index curled behind the stem with its tip hidden, middle, ring
  and little fingers wrapped round with their tips returning toward the
  viewer. The dark wedge inside the fist is a good linocut device; keep it.
- The stem is continuous: it enters under the thumb and leaves under the
  little finger on one axis.
- The bowl is the app icon's bowl, swirl up the right side, one cream sliver
  as the highlight. That is already the brief's exposed-garment highlight.
- The wider foot, about 80% of bowl width, reads as a foot rather than a pin.

Corrections:

1. **Foot tangent to the wrist.** The foot's left tip lands on the wrist
   outline. The foot is in front of the wrist, so overlap the wrist clearly
   and interrupt the wrist line behind it, by about a tenth of the foot's
   width. (A clear gap is the alternative; it reads as floating.)
2. **Foot and rim disagree about eye level.** The rim is almost edge-on, the
   foot an open ellipse seen from above. Flatten the foot ellipse to about
   three fifths of its current height at the same width. The icon's rim is
   near edge-on too, so flatten the foot rather than open the rim.
3. **Stem exit.** A small flare under the little finger reads as a knop.
   One stem, one width, to the foot.
4. **Scale is poster scale; keep it.** The glass is about 1.5× life against
   this hand. That is what gives the stem room for three fingers and keeps
   the bowl the hero. The illustrator must not "correct" it; recorded as an
   invariant in the brief.

Notes, not corrections: this is an outline drawing, not yet a linocut; the
cuts, the hatching on the hand and the wrist bone come at the vector stage per
the brief. The three square fingernails are a little cartoon; each becomes one
nick in the cut version.
